08/07.08.2025  I.A. No.5018 of 2021 This interlocutory application has been filed for grant for bail in connection with S.T. No.217 of 2013 arising out of Saraiyahat (Hannsdiha) P.S. Case No.226 of 2012, corresponding to G.R. Case No.1298 of 2012 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge-II-cum-F.T.C. for Offences Against Women, Dumka, holding the appellant guilty for offences under Sections 302/34, 376(2)(g) and 201/34 of the I.P.C. and thereby sentencing him to undergo imprisonment for life for offence under Section 302/34 of the I.P.C. along with fine, R.I. for three years for the offence under Sections 201/34 of the I.P.C. along with fine and R.I. for 12 years for the offence under Section 376(2)(g) of the I.P.C. along with fine.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-II-cum-F.T.C. for Offences Against Women, Dumka
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Earlier this interlocutory application was heard by another Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court.
There was difference of opinion between the Hon'ble Judges on the point of suspension of sentence of the appellant.

It appears that Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay had passed an order directing the appellant to be released on bail, considering his period of incarceration and also considering the fact that similarly situated co- convicts have been granted bail earlier by different co-ordinate benches of this court.
However, Hon'ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Prasad had rejected the interlocutory application on merit.
As per the prosecution case, the deceased Maneshwar Sao and his wife were abducted by unknown persons.
Later on, dead body of Maneshwar Sao was recovered.

entities.text: Chandra Kishor Rana vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The victim has been examined as P.W. 9.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant submitted that appellant has remained in custody for 12  years.
It was further submitted that similarly situated co-convicts have been granted bail by different Co- ordinate Division Benches of this Court on the ground of their period of incarceration.
The appellant is in custody for more than 12 years and other co- convicts have been released on bail.
The hearing of this appeal is not likely to be taken up in near future.

Considering his period of custody, the appellant Chandra Kishor Rana is also directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees twenty thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II-cum-F.T.C. Offences Against Women, Dumka,
in connection with S.T. No.217 of 2013 arising out of Saraiyahat (Hannsdiha) P.S. Case No.226 of 2012, corresponding to G.R. Case No.1298 of 2012.
The aforesaid interlocutory application is allowed.

(Ambuj Nath, J.) Jay/-
